title: Liberalism in IR: Pathways to Peace

scenes.text: Can ordinary people and trade stop wars between rival countries?
scenes.narration: Realists argue that war is inevitable under global anarchy. But imagine if people, trade, and shared democracy can actually build lasting peace!

scenes.text: Friendly neighbors share garden tools and build trust before settling property disputes.
scenes.narration: Think of two rival neighbors as an analogy. Instead of arguing over boundary walls first, they share garden tools, chat over tea, and gradually build trust.

scenes.name: Karl Deutsch
scenes.idea: Cross-border communication and travel build a peaceful security community.
scenes.narration: Here's the trick: sociological liberalism looks beyond governments. Karl Deutsch showed that regular phone calls, letters, and travel create a security community where war becomes unthinkable.

scenes.heading: Billiard Balls Versus Cobweb
scenes.narration: Notice how John Burton rejected the old billiard ball model of hard states. Instead, imagine world order as a cobweb of crisscrossing social ties that bypass governments.

scenes.heading: Peace by Pieces Process
scenes.narration: David Mitrany proposed functionalism: building peace by pieces. Technicians handle low politics first, sparking spillover into deeper integration, though Ernst Haas warned political will is needed to sustain it.

scenes.name: Michael Doyle
scenes.idea: Democracies do not fight each other and form a zone of peace.
scenes.narration: Now meet democratic peace theory. Michael Doyle argued that democracies do not fight each other because voting citizens, free speech, and mutual tolerance restrain aggressive leaders.

scenes.heading: Democratic Peace Theory Debate
scenes.narration: Weigh both sides carefully. While democracies form a peaceful zone, critics warn the theory was used to justify armed regime change in Iraq, showing democracy promotion carries real risks.

items: Sociological ties create Deutsch's security community
Functional spillover builds cooperation through technical experts
Democratic peace theory restrains war between free societies
scenes.narration: Here's your quick recap! Sociological ties build security communities, functional spillover creates habits of cooperation, and democratic norms help keep the peace between free nations.
